answer: Negative example for every p>2 and d>=3
evidence: Published JEMS27(2025),4845–4890, DOI10.4171/JEMS/1462; EMS confirms acceptance26September2022 and online publication23April2024. Actual46page journal PDF retrieved and theorem/construction interface read. Product-domain reduction independently proved.
locators: Theorem1.2 printed p.4847; restatement Theorem9.4 and construction interface pp.4886–4888.
audit: The actual theorem supplies, for every p>1 other than2, a continuous planar distributional p-harmonic u in W^(1,p-1+epsilon), with infinite p-energy on every nonempty open subdomain. In particular for p>2 its local gradient and u belong to L^(p-1), and the nonlinear flux is L1. Theorem9.4 repeats the same claim; its strong-gradient limit and constitutive-inclusion passage have the stated interface. To match d>=3 choose Omega=B×(0,1)^(d-2) and U(x,z)=u(x), where B is the source ball. The weak gradient is (grad u,0); finite local product measure gives W^(1,p-1)_loc. For any smooth compactly supported test, integration over z produces a smooth compactly supported planar test; Fubini is valid for the L1 flux and reduces the equation exactly to the planar distributional equation. A product of compactly contained nonempty open sets has p-energy equal to its positive transverse volume times the infinite planar energy by Tonelli. Thus U is not locally W^(1,p), and changing representatives cannot change its weak gradient. There is no dimension or endpoint-integrability mismatch. This is an actual published counterexample plus an elementary extension, not an unreviewed new endpoint conjecture.
